jobs.summary: Full-Time Urology PA/NP at Tufts Medical Center. Setting: mixed settings.
jobs.description:
At Tufts Medicine, you’ll make an impact and build your career, supported by a community of brilliant, compassionate colleagues. Every single person at Tufts Medicine plays an integral role in building a holistic healthcare experience that’s accessible, empowering and, most of all, human.

Tufts Medicine Lowell General Hospital and Merrimack Urology Associates are seeking a full-time Inpatient Urology Physician Assistant (PA) or Nurse Practitioner (NP) to join our collaborative urology team. This position will provide inpatient urologic care across our Main and Saints Campuses, which are conveniently located approximately 1.5 miles apart.

Work Schedule:

• Four days per week: Monday–Thursday, 2:00 p.m.–12:00 a.m.

Department of Urology Overview:

Integrated Healthcare: Merrimack Urology Associates is a well-established practice located in Chelmsford, Massachusetts. After 50-years of independent practice, Merrimack Urology Associates merged with Lowell General Hospital in 2021, which is part of Tuts Medicine Health System with over 700 affiliated doctors and a clinical affliction with Tufts Medical Center.

Academics: As part of Tufts Medicine, Lowell General Hospital offers the opportunity to have an academic appointment within Tufts University School of Medicine, with a wide variety of teaching activities available.

Our Practice: Merrimack Urology Associates practices nearly all aspects of Urology, including oncology, endoscopic stone procedures, laparoscopy and robotics, MRI guided prostate biopsies, incontinence, erectile dysfunction, BPH, female urology, and basic pediatric urology.

Collaboration: Our team currently consists of five full-time physicians and three full-time Nurse Practitioners. Our practice serves a large and diverse community.

Responsibilities:

You will serve as a member of a large and diverse team in an outpatient setting, working collaboratively with a multidisciplinary team to provide cutting-edge and patient-focused care.

• Community Setting. Provide specialty and subspecialty care to the Greater Lowell community, known for their vibrancy, access to cultural, historical and outdoor attractions and close access to Boston.
• Patient Focus. Our integrated network allows for increased access to care for our patients, with collaborations that extend beyond our four walls, including our association with an excellent Cancer Center running trials in partnership with Dana Farber and other Boston-area Hospitals
• Teamwork. Multidisciplinary support with Interventional Radiology, Nephrology, Oncology and others.
• State of the art. We perform office-based cystoscopies, TRUS Bx’s, vasectomies and offer in-house ultrasounds performed by certified sonographers. Our only OR is located at Lowell General Hospital’s Main Campus, offering a state-of-the-art Endourology Suite, a DaVinci Xi Robot, and dedicated Urology staff with easy access to MRI guided prostate biopsies and ESWLs.

Requirements:

• Graduate of an accredited and/or approved Physician Assistant or Nurse Practitioner program
• Current license as a Physician Assistant or Nurse Practitioner in the Commonwealth of Massachusetts
• Background in Urology through prior advanced practice experience, or clinical rotations
• Current certification in CPR
• A team player who is excited to work cooperatively with a wide range of stakeholders and disciplines to champions world class patient satisfaction and support

Apply: Please submit application/CV via this job post or email CV directly to David Rezendes, Physician Recruiter, at David.Rezendes@tuftsmedicine.org.

About Tufts Medicine:

Tufts Medicine is a leading integrated health system bringing together the best of academic and community healthcare to deliver exceptional, connected and accessible care experiences to consumers across Massachusetts. Comprised of Tufts Medical Center, Lowell General Hospital, MelroseWakefield Hospital, Lawrence Memorial Hospital of Medford, Care at Home - an expansive home care network, and large integrated physician network.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity and inclusion at Tufts Medicine. Tufts Medicine does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, national origin, gender identity and/or expression, marital status or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law.

We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment.

At Tufts Medicine, we want every individual to feel valued for the skills and experience they bring. Our compensation philosophy is designed to offer fair, competitive pay that attracts, retains, and motivates highly talented individuals, while rewarding the important work you do every day.

The base pay ranges reflect the minimum qualifications for the role. Individual offers are determined using a comprehensive approach that considers relevant experience, certifications, education, skills, and internal equity to ensure compensation is fair, consistent, and aligned with our business goals.

Beyond base pay, Tufts Medicine provides a comprehensive Total Rewards package that supports your health, financial security, and career growth—one of the many ways we invest in you so you can thrive both at work and outside of it.

Atrium Health Levine Children's Hospital is seeking an APP to join our growing Pediatric Preventive Cardiology program, part of Advocate Health.

This is a primarily clinical outpatient role focused on the assessment and longitudinal management of children and adolescents with cardiovascular risk factors and conditions that predispose to early cardiovascular disease, with opportunities to participate in research and program development. The successful candidate will deliver care across both in-person and virtual clinics, supporting patients and families throughout North Carolina, South Carolina, and Georgia.

About the Program

Our Pediatric Preventive Cardiology program—based at Levine Children's Hospital and supported by the resources of Advocate Health, one of the nation's largest integrated health systems—provides specialized, evidence-based care aimed at identifying and modifying cardiovascular risk early in life.

The patient population includes children and adolescents with:

· Hypertension and elevated blood pressure

· Familial hypercholesterolemia (heterozygous and homozygous), including cascade-screened family members

· Hypertriglyceridemia and rare genetic dyslipidemias

· Elevated cardiovascular risk secondary to high-risk conditions, including childhood cancer survivors, chronic kidney disease, and inflammatory/autoimmune disorders

The program operates through a hybrid model of in-person clinics and telehealth, expanding access to specialized preventive care across a three-state region.

Key Responsibilities

This is a predominantly clinical position. The majority of the role is dedicated to direct patient care, with protected opportunities for research and program development available to candidates with those interests.

Clinical Care (primary focus)

· Provide comprehensive outpatient evaluation and longitudinal management for the patient populations described above, in collaboration with attending pediatric cardiologists.

· Conduct new-patient evaluations, follow-up visits, lipid and blood pressure management, lifestyle counseling, and pharmacologic management as appropriate.

· Order and interpret relevant diagnostic studies (e.g., lipid panels, ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, echocardiography, and other cardiovascular testing) in coordination with the care team.

· Deliver care through both in-person clinics and virtual/telehealth visits to patients located across North Carolina, South Carolina, and Georgia.

· Provide patient- and family-centered education, including on diet, physical activity, medication adherence, and condition-specific risk reduction.

· Coordinate care with referring providers, primary care, and subspecialists (oncology, nephrology, rheumatology, genetics), as well as community resources.

Research (opportunity)

· Participate in clinical and quality-improvement research within the program, with opportunities to contribute to study design, data collection, and dissemination.

· Support outcomes tracking across the patient population.

Program Development (opportunity)

· Contribute to the development and refinement of clinical pathways and protocols, with a specific focus on the outpatient management of pediatric hypertension.

· Help build and standardize workflows, documentation tools, and care models that scale across in-person and virtual settings and across multiple states.

Qualifications

· Master's or Doctoral degree from an accredited Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant program.

· Current certification as a Physician Assistant ( PA-C) or Pediatric Nurse Practitioner (PNP-PC or PNP-AC) or Family Nurse Practitioner (FNP) with relevant pediatric experience.

· Active, unrestricted PA/NP licensure with eligibility to obtain and maintain authorization to practice in North Carolina, South Carolina, and Georgia (multi-state licensure is required to support cross-state telehealth and in-person care).

· DEA registration or eligibility.

Ideal Candidate

· Clinical experience in pediatric cardiology, preventive cardiology, lipidology, or management of pediatric hypertension.

· Experience with telehealth delivery and comfort managing patients across a hybrid in-person/virtual model.

· Familiarity with chronic disease management in high-risk pediatric populations (e.g., cancer survivorship, chronic kidney disease, inflammatory disorders).

· Interest or prior experience in clinical research, quality improvement, or program development.

Practice Setting

This position combines in-person clinic sessions with virtual care, allowing flexible delivery of specialized preventive cardiology services to patients across a three-state catchment area. The role is well suited to a clinician who values direct patient care and the chance to help shape a developing program within an academic children's hospital environment.

Atrium Health is seeking an experienced, full-time Advanced Practice Provider specializing in Behavioral Health to provide comprehensive psychiatric and behavioral health services within our Emergency Department and Psychiatric Observation Unit.

This hybrid position is open to board-certified Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioners (PMHNP-BC) and Physician Assistants (PA) who are trained and proficient in the delivery of psychiatric services. The provider will perform in-person and virtual psychiatric evaluations, medication management, and treatment services for patients experiencing acute and chronic mental health and substance use disorders.

The Behavioral Health Advanced Practice Provider provides specialized psychiatric evaluation, consultation, stabilization, and treatment services to patients experiencing acute and chronic behavioral health conditions within Atrium Health’s Emergency Department and Psychiatric Observation Unit.

The provider will conduct in-person and virtual psychiatric evaluations, assess and diagnose psychiatric conditions, manage medications, and develop individualized treatment recommendations to support patient safety, stabilization, and appropriate disposition. Patient populations may include individuals experiencing depression, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, substance use disorders, and withdrawal-related psychiatric symptoms.

Working in collaboration with psychiatrists, emergency medicine providers, nursing staff, social workers, case managers, and other healthcare professionals, the APP will facilitate timely access to psychiatric services, promote effective care coordination, and support safe transitions across levels of care.

This hybrid position provides essential behavioral health coverage during variable day and evening shifts, including weekends and holidays, contributing to continuity of care, improved patient access, and efficient clinical workflows within the psychiatric emergency department.

Job Summary: Provides direct patient care relative to physical diagnosis and therapeutic management independently, using physician consultation where appropriate.

Job Description:

Essential Responsibilities:

Assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation of the plan of care for a panel of patients. Evaluates individual health care status of patients, including eliciting a patient history, performance of physical examination, ordering of screening and diagnostic tests, risk assessment and interprets this information to establish a diagnosis.

Develops and implements a plan of care, including treatments, medications and the like within defined guidelines for practice. Provides care to the patient in a manner that incorporates the principles of patient satisfaction and delivery of cost effective care. Participates in the development and evaluation of practice guidelines.

Monitors the individual's response to therapy and revises the plan, as indicated, with particular attention to education and counseling and encouragement of self-care. Provides ongoing individualized patient orientation to APG/BIDCO. Seeks consultation from the consulting physician and other members of the healthcare team. Makes appropriate referrals as indicated by patient needs.

Identifies learning needs of patients and staff and collaborates with other leaders to determine priorities for educational programs. Participates in interdisciplinary education programs of the practice and provides clinical precepting for nursing students, nurse practitioner students, medical students and others. Provides leadership that supports APG, BIDHC practice policies and goals.

Required Qualifications:

Master's degree in Nursing required.

License Nursing License required., and Certificate 1 Basic Life Support required.

1-3 years related work experience required.

Valid prescriptive authority from both the MA DPH-DCP and Federal DEA

MA Board authorization to practice as an APRN NRSG

American Heart Association-Basic Life Support Certificate

Experience with computer systems required, including web based applications and some Microsoft Office applications which may include Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint or Access.

Preferred Qualifications:

Related primary care practice expertise.

Competencies:

Written Communications: Ability to summarize and communicate in English moderately complex information in varied written formats to internal and external customers.

Oral Communications: Ability to comprehend and communicate complex verbal information in English to medical center staff, patients, families and external customers.

Knowledge: Ability to demonstrate in-depth knowledge of concepts, practices and policies with the ability to use them in complex varied situations.

Team Work: Ability to lead collaborative teams for larger projects or groups both internal and external to the Medical Center and across functional areas. Results have implications for the management and operations of multiple areas of the organization.

Customer Service: Ability to provide a high level of customer service and staff training to meet customer service standards and expectations for the assigned unit(s). Resolves service issues in the assigned unit(s) in a timely and respectful manner.

Age based Competencies:
Employees in this job must be competent to provide patient care to the following age groups: Neonatal:Birth to 6 months, Youth: 6 months to 16 years, Young adult: 16-30 years, Middle Age: 30 - 60 years, Elderly: 60 -.
Physical Nature of the Job:
Medium work: Exerting up to 50 pounds of force occasionally and or up to 20 pounds of force frequently. Job is physical in nature and employee needs to stand and/or move around through the majority of their shift.

$84,349.20 USD - $109,948.80 USD

jobs.description:
When you join the growing BILH team, you're not just taking a job, you’re making a difference in people’s lives.

Schedule

This is a full-time, 40-hour position. You'll work four 10-hour shifts each week, with a combination of operating room time and independent clinic sessions. Typically, you'll spend 1-2 days assisting in surgery and the remainder of the week managing your own clinic schedule. There are no nights, weekends, or call responsibilities.

Where You'll Work

The primary clinic location will be in Chestnut Hill, where you'll see patients in an outpatient setting. Surgical cases are performed primarily at New England Baptist Hospital in Mission Hill, with future opportunities to support procedures at the expanding surgical center at One Brookline Place. You'll be part of a large, collaborative Orthopaedics APP team of approximately 20 Advanced Practice Providers spanning a wide range of subspecialties.

What You'll Do

As an Orthopaedic NP/PA, you'll partner closely with a surgeon whose practice includes general Orthopaedics, sports-related procedures, shoulder replacement surgery, and total knee replacements. You'll assist in the operating room and independently manage your own outpatient clinic schedule, seeing the surgeon's patients for post-operative visits, follow-up care, evaluations, and injections. While you'll often practice alongside the attending physician in the same clinic space, you'll maintain your own patient panel and schedule, providing a high level of autonomous care with direct physician support readily available when needed.

Why You'll Love Working Here

This role offers the best of both worlds: meaningful surgical experience and the opportunity to build strong patient relationships through independent clinical practice. You'll join a highly respected and collegial Orthopaedics team that values APP autonomy, collaboration, and professional growth. With a diverse patient population, exposure to a broad range of Orthopaedic conditions and procedures, an experienced physician partner, and a schedule free from call, nights, and weekends, you'll have the opportunity to practice at the top of your license while maintaining excellent work-life balance.

When you join the growing BILH team, you're not just taking a job, you’re making a difference in people’s lives.

This position is full time, 40 hours per week, 5 8-hour shifts. No nights, weekends, or major holidays. The clinic is located at 725 Concord Ave in Cambridge.

About Our Practice

Mount Auburn OB/GYN is a busy, collaborative outpatient practice located at our Fresh Pond location. As part of a nationally recognized maternity care program, we are proud to partner closely with physicians and one of the largest midwifery practices in Eastern Massachusetts to provide comprehensive, patient-centered care across the lifespan.

Our team is dedicated to delivering high-quality obstetric and gynecologic care in a supportive environment that values collaboration, compassion, and clinical excellence.

The Role

As a Nurse Practitioner, you will provide direct patient care in a fast-paced ambulatory setting, caring for a diverse patient population across both obstetrics and gynecology. Responsibilities include managing patient needs, conducting annual visits, caring for obstetric patients, and providing follow-up gynecologic care.

Working alongside physicians and midwives, you will play an integral role in ensuring timely access to care while delivering exceptional patient experiences and outcomes.

Why Mount Auburn?

At Mount Auburn Hospital, you'll join a respected and growing team committed to providing outstanding care to the communities we serve. Our collaborative practice model, strong physician and midwifery partnerships, and commitment to patient-centered care create an environment where advanced practice providers can thrive.

If you are passionate about obstetric and gynecologic care and enjoy working in a dynamic outpatient setting, Mount Auburn offers the opportunity to make a meaningful impact while growing your clinical expertise.

Carilion Clinic is seeking a skilled and collaborative Advanced Practice Provider (Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant) to join our General Surgery team. This APP will work as an integral member of a busy surgical practice supporting a team of 13 general surgeons and providing high-quality, patient-centered care across the surgical continuum.

Position Overview

The General Surgery APP will partner closely with surgeons, nursing staff, and other members of the multidisciplinary care team to support efficient, coordinated care for general surgery patients. The position offers a four-day workweek consisting of four 10-hour shifts, providing a balance of meaningful clinical responsibility, professional collaboration, and schedule flexibility.

The ideal candidate is an APP who thrives in a team-based environment, communicates effectively, demonstrates sound clinical judgment, and is comfortable managing the needs of a diverse general surgery patient population.

Provide comprehensive care for general surgery patients in collaboration with the general surgeons.

• Perform patient evaluations, histories and physical examinations, and develop appropriate assessment and treatment plans.
• Participate in preoperative and postoperative patient management.
• Evaluate postoperative concerns, identify complications, and coordinate care with the surgical team.
• Order and interpret appropriate laboratory studies, imaging, and other diagnostic testing within scope of practice.
• Provide patient and family education regarding surgical procedures, recovery, wound care, medications, and follow-up.
• Assist with clinical procedures within training, credentialing, and scope of practice.
• Facilitate timely communication among surgeons, nursing teams, consultants, and other members of the care team.
• Support continuity of care, patient throughput, and timely follow-up for the General Surgery service.
• Maintain accurate and timely clinical documentation.
• Participate in quality improvement, patient safety, and practice-efficiency initiatives.

Qualifications:

• Strong clinical assessment, communication, organizational, and decision-making skills.
• Ability to work effectively within a large, collaborative surgical team.

Sturdy Health is seeking a FT Gastroenterology Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant to join our well-established and successful team at our outpatient office in Attleboro, MA.

We are committed to providing the highest quality health care to adult patients. With convenient office hours and quick access to major highways, it is easy for our patients to get quality health care locally.

Our gastroenterologists care for a wide variety of patients, including those with gastroesophageal reflux (GERD), Barrett's esophagus, esophageal motility disorders, H. pylori infection, acute and chronic liver disease, and inflammatory bowel disease.

We have close relationships with our community-based primary care physicians, other specialists, and hospital staff - all with the main goal of providing personalized, comprehensive digestive health care in the hospital and office-based setting.

About the job:

• Provide direct patient care to our communities with a well-established practice
• Patient-centric mindset to provide the highest-quality service and patient care
• Work alongside passionate gastroenterologists and advanced practitioners
• Grow as a clinician as you learn from experienced colleagues
• Work cross-functionally with primary care providers
• Full-time employment preferred
• Primarily outpatient position
• Brand new ambulatory office space being built on the hospital campus

Requirements:

• Graduate of an accredited and/or approved Adult/Gerontology Nurse Practitioner, Family Medicine Nurse Practitioner, or Physician Assistant Program
• Current license as a Registered Nurse and Nurse Practitioner, or Physician Assistant, in the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, or ability to obtain
• Must have or eligible for, and maintain, a current DEA registration and Massachusetts Controlled Substance Registration
• Current certification in CPR required
• Requires a minimum of 1 to 2 years’ experience in Gastroenterology as a Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant
• Interested in working full time, preferred

Location: 150 Emory Street, Attleboro, MA

Comprehensive Benefits: We offer a competitive salary with comprehensive benefits including medical, dental, and vision insurance options, and more.

• Guaranteed base salary with productivity-based incentive
• Professional liability insurance
• 4 weeks PTO, 1 week CME, and 10 paid holidays
• Reimbursement stipend for CME expenses, memberships and dues, licensure and DEA fees
• Retirement plans including employer-paid pension plan, 403B plan with employer match

Contact: Please submit your application materials through the link on this page. For any questions, please contact Kelly Fitzpatrick at KFitzpatrick@sturdyhealth.org

Located in Attleboro, MA, Sturdy Health is an integrated health care system that offers hospital-based care, emergency care, urgent care, primary care, and a wide range of specialty care at 26 ambulatory locations throughout our region.

Sturdy Memorial Hospital is an independent, financially stable, acute care, 142-bed community hospital. We serve a population base of 170,000 in suburban communities of Boston and Providence. Attleboro is within 25 minutes of Boston and 15 minutes of Providence, RI.

Excellent operation of clinical equipment

jobs.summary: UVA Pediatrics Culpeper - Pediatric Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant- Full Time at UVA Health Children's. Setting: pediatric primary care. Notable: loan repayment.
jobs.description:
UVA Pediatrics Culpeper is seeking a full-time Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant that specializes in primary care pediatrics.

Position Highlights
Practice Hours: Monday - Thursday 8 am - 6 pm, Friday 8 am - 5pm, Saturday 8:30 am - 1 pm
Schedule is 4, 10 hour days Monday - Friday with rotating Saturday hours
Saturday clinic coverage (typically once every 6-7 weeks)
Rotating call coverage
Outpatient only
Practice offers both primary care and same-day appointment visits
Public Service Loan Forgiveness eligible organization

Responsible for provision of Advanced Practice Provider services, including assessment and management of patients across all clinical settings, (examples: ambulatory clinic, hospital, assisted living facility, skilled nursing facility/nursing home, ambulatory surgery center, and community settings), within the scope of licensing, training, and credentialing dependent on specialty.

• Works in conjunction with the medical director, administrative management, nursing and other interprofessional team members to facilitate patient care and management throughout the health care system.
• Exercises independent judgment in the assessment, diagnosis and initiation of medical processes and procedures commensurate with training and experience, as credentialed by UVA Health System.
• Performs and documents comprehensive health histories and physical assessments, to include initiation of CPR or other appropriate emergency therapy as needed.
• Formulates diagnoses, identifies problems and health risk profiles, documents and clearly communicates with other members of the health care team.
• Performs, orders, and interprets diagnostic studies, such as x-rays and laboratory tests, in consultation with peers and colleagues.
• Performs procedures within scope of practice and UVA Health System credentialing and privileges.
• Orders medications, treatments and therapies in accordance with Virginia Prescriptive regulations.
• Requests consultation and initiates referrals to other health care providers, including specialists when and if needed.
• Evaluates and analyzes patient responses to the disease process and/or therapeutic, diagnostic interventions.
• Provides information, education and support to patients/families regarding disease processes and treatment plans (diagnostic procedures, medications and treatments), thus facilitating communication between patients/families and the health care team.
• Participates in on-call responsibilities as appropriate and as determined by department or unit.
• Manages patients in accordance with established UVA Medical Center and UVA UPG policies and procedures.
• Reports births, deaths, outbreaks of communicable diseases and other information critical to the patient’s and/or the public’s health as required by legal or governmental authorities, in a timely manner.
• Meets quality standards as determined by the Medical Director and/or UVA Health System.
• May serve on select committees as needed.
• May participate in the clinical experience of students (graduate/post graduate advanced practice, nursing, and medical students), interns, and residents, as appropriate.
• Participates in group, peer and other review activities as requested.
• Prepares and attends to all reports, claims, and correspondence necessary or appropriate to the performance of professional services.
• Promotes the professional practice of the advanced practice group by serving as a clinical resource to nursing, medical and allied health care practitioners.
• Follows policies and procedures, including those of UPG, UVA Medical Center, CMS and other contracted payers with which the entity may contract.
• Accurately assigns Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) and International Classification of Diseases (ICD-10), codes.
• Updates practice through continuing education by attending conferences, rounds, reports, lectures, journal clubs and regional/national professional conferences.
• Seeks professional development and growth opportunities that enhance professional practice through formal and informal activities including developing and presenting educational programs.
• Performs other duties as assigned that are commensurate with professional service normally and customarily provided by a licensed independent provider.

COMPENSATION

• During the first two years of employment, the provider will receive a tiered base salary plus a $10,000 guaranteed incentive.
• Following the completion of the two-year guarantee period, compensation will transition to a tiered base salary plus a wRVU-based incentive model.

Base salary is determined by years of APP experience:

• 0–5 years of experience: $105,000 base salary
• More than 5 years up to 10 years of experience: $115,000 base salary
• More than 10 years of experience: $125,000 base salary

UVA Physicians Group Benefit Highlights

• Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance options.
• Employer-sponsored retirement savings plans with employer contributions and pre-tax/Roth savings options.
• Generous paid time off, paid holidays, and leave benefits.
• Employer-paid life insurance, short-term disability, and long-term disability coverage.
• CME/professional development support
• Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) eligibility for many positions.

Education: Graduate of an accredited graduate school of nursing or physician assistant program with a master’s degree.
Experience: Department and unit specific.

jobs.summary: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (Autonomous Licensed) - PMH NP -UVA Augusta Pediatrics - (VIRTUAL POSITION) at UVA Health Children's. Setting: mixed settings. Notable: loan repayment.
jobs.description:
UVA Augusta Pediatrics is seeking an experienced and autonomously licensed, Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP) to provide outpatient behavioral health services within a collaborative pediatric primary care setting. This full-time virtual position offers a four-day workweek (4 x 10-hour shifts) with no inpatient responsibilities. Experience with pediatrics/ teens and young adults ages 5 and up. For this position, there would be some required onsite meetings, collaboration and networking to ensure the role is fully integrated with the clinic teams and workflows. However, patient visits would be conducted virtually.

Responsible for provision of Advanced Practice Provider services, including assessment and management of patients across all clinical settings, within the scope of licensing, training, and credentialing dependent on specialty.

Virtual Delivery Requirements

• Must reside in Virginia and deliver all care from within the Commonwealth
• Reliable high-speed internet required for video-based patient care
• Computer equipment will be provided
• Private, confidential workspace suitable for clinical telehealth

Schedule

• 32 patient-facing hours per week plus 8 hours of administrative time (total 40 hours)
• Schedule could include weekend and/or evening coverage as needed and based on patient needs.
• Flexibility is essential to success in this role.

Position Highlights

• No hospital call or inpatient coverage
• Integrated behavioral health model within a pediatric primary care practice
• Collaborative support from pediatric primary care providers, nursing, and care management teams

Key Responsibilities

• Conduct comprehensive psychiatric evaluations and diagnostic assessments for pediatrics, adolescents and young adults.
• Diagnose and treat a broad range of mental health conditions, including depression, anxiety, ADHD, autism, PTSD, bipolar disorder, and other psychiatric disorders.
• Develop individualized treatment plans utilizing evidence-based medication management and therapeutic interventions.
• Prescribe, adjust and monitor psychotropic medications in accordance with Virginia regulations and clinical best practices.
• Provide ongoing follow-up care, including symptom management, treatment monitoring and medication education.
• Collaborate closely with pediatric primary care providers to support integrated patient care and address behavioral health needs within the pediatric primary care setting.
• Coordinate referrals to specialty behavioral health services, counseling, substance use treatment, and community resources as appropriate.
• Maintain accurate and timely documentation in the electronic medical record.
• Participate in quality improvement initiatives and contribute to a patient-centered, team-based care environment.

Qualifications

• Master's or Doctoral degree from an accredited Nurse Practitioner program.
• Board certification as a Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP).
• Current or eligible Virginia Nurse Practitioner and Registered Nurse licensure.
• DEA registration and prescriptive authority eligibility.
• Minimum of 3 years of psychiatric practice experience in pediatrics.
• Ability to practice independently and manage a diverse outpatient psychiatric patient panel.

COMPENSATION

• Tiered base salary plus a productivity (wRVU)-based incentive model.
• Base salary is determined by years of APP experience:
• 0–5 years of experience: $105,000 base salary
• More than 5 years up to 10 years of experience: $115,000 base salary
• More than 10 years of experience: $125,000 base salary

UVA Physicians Group Benefit Highlights

• Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance options.
• Employer-sponsored retirement savings plans with employer contributions and pre-tax/Roth savings options.
• Generous paid time off, paid holidays, and leave benefits.
• Employer-paid life insurance, short-term disability, and long-term disability coverage.
• CME/professional development support
• Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) eligibility for many positions.
